errors.location: RF-EMR exposure effects on learning and memory
errors.description: The text identifies Son et al.’s subjects as rats, but reference 56 identifies the study as using 5xFAD mice. This misreports the study population.
errors.evidence: Text: “in a research conducted on rats by Son et al”; reference 56 title: “Long-term RF exposure on behavior and cerebral glucose metabolism in 5xFAD mice.”

errors.location: ELF-EMF section, paragraph on Ahlbom et al.’s pooled analysis
errors.description: The account appears to treat the proportions of children in exposure categories as evidence about their relative risks. Exposure prevalence alone does not establish risk; the text supplies no case/control counts or effect estimates supporting that inference.
errors.evidence: “99.2% of children residing in households with exposure levels below 0.4 μT exhibited a lower risk… In contrast, 0.8% of children exposed to 0.4 μT or higher displayed relatively elevated risk estimates.”

errors.location: Paragraph beginning “The nonthermal effects arise from forces acting on particles”
errors.description: The text generalizes that nonthermal effects arise from the pearl-chain effect, then identifies dielectric saturation as another nonthermal effect. Those statements are internally inconsistent: the latter is presented as a distinct mechanism, not as pearl-chain formation.
errors.evidence: “The nonthermal effects arise from forces acting on particles, known as the pearl chain effect.” Later: “Another nonthermal effect is the dielectric saturation…”
